questions.stem: Two spherical raindrops of equal size fall through air with terminal velocity of $10\ \mathrm{cm/s}$. If they coalesce to form a single drop, its terminal velocity will be:
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity $v_t \propto r^2$.
When two drops of radius $r$ coalesce, the volume is doubled:
$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 2 \left(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right) \implies R = 2^{1/3} r$.
Since $v_t \propto r^2$, the new terminal velocity is $v_t' = v_t \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2 = 10 \times (2^{1/3})^2 = 10 \times 2^{2/3}\ \mathrm{cm/s}$.

questions.stem: Eight identical spherical raindrops falling down with terminal velocity $v$ merge to form a single large drop. The terminal velocity of the new large drop is:
questions.solution:
Volume remains conserved: $8 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \implies R = 2r$.
Terminal velocity $v_T \propto r^2$. Therefore, $v' = v \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2 = v(2)^2 = 4v$.
